strategies.name: Swap-Spread Arbitrage
strategies.rule_summary: Go long (short) a fixed-for-floating interest rate swap, receiving (paying) the fixed swap rate against LIBOR. At the same time, short (buy) a Treasury bond with the same maturity, financed at the repo rate, so the position is dollar-neutral. P&L accrues at ±[(swap rate − Treasury yield) − (LIBOR − repo rate)]. The long-swap version pays off if LIBOR falls, so the trade is a bet on LIBOR.
strategies.backtest_note: The text gives no rule for choosing the long or short side and no rule for entering or exiting the trade, and you need OTC swap rates and repo rate data to test it.
data_sources: GAP: CDS spreads / swap rates history
gaps: OTC instruments; no source

strategies.name: Cash-and-carry Arbitrage
strategies.rule_summary: Compute the fair futures price F* = (S − D)·exp(r(T−t)), where D is the discounted value of dividends paid before delivery. The basis is B = (F − F*)/S. If |B| is larger than transaction costs, sell the futures and buy the index basket when B > 0, or buy the futures and short the basket when B < 0. Close the position when the basis returns to zero.
strategies.backtest_note: These opportunities last only a short time and need synchronized high-frequency data, dividend forecasts and realistic slippage/execution modelling, so results depend heavily on those assumptions.
data_sources: IBKR history (index futures and ETF/basket bars)
gaps: Fair basis needs dividends and financing rates

strategies.name: Dispersion Trading in Equity Indexes
strategies.name_es: Trading de dispersión en índices de acciones
strategies.rule_summary: Buy near-ATM straddles on each index constituent and sell one near-ATM straddle on the index. Hold n_i = S_i*P_I / sum_j(S_j*P_j) straddles on stock i, where S_i is shares outstanding and the index is cap-weighted. The trade is put on when index implied volatility is well above the theoretical index volatility, which is computed from the constituent implied volatilities and the historical correlation matrix. All options have about 1 month to expiry, and the positions are held until expiry.
required_data: option chains with implied volatility for index and constituents
daily close prices for historical correlations
strategies.backtest_note: The text gives no numeric entry threshold or correlation lookback, and you need full option data for every constituent, which is expensive to get.
data_sources: GAP: historical option chains for index and constituents
gaps: Needs option quotes for the index and its members

strategies.name: Dispersion Trading: Subset Portfolio
strategies.name_es: Trading de dispersión – subconjunto del portafolio
strategies.rule_summary: Sell ATM straddles on the index (e.g. S&P 500) when its implied volatility is above the theoretical index volatility, and buy ATM straddles on only a subset of the constituent stocks. Theoretical index volatility uses a statistical risk model correlation matrix: keep the top K principal components of the sample correlation matrix (e.g. daily close-to-close returns over 1 year, about 252 days), with K set by eRank, and add a specific-risk diagonal. The long leg holds straddles on the N* stocks with the lowest specific-risk contribution w_i^2 σ_i^2 ξ_i^2 (e.g. N* = 100 for the S&P 500).
strategies.backtest_note: The text does not give straddle sizing, maturity or exit rules, and you need historical option implied-volatility data for every constituent stock.
data_sources: GAP: historical option chains for index and constituents
gaps: Needs option quotes for the index and its members

strategies.name: Intraday Arbitrage Between Index ETFs
strategies.name_es: Arbitraje intradía entre ETFs de índices
strategies.rule_summary: Trade two ETFs that track the same index, for example SPY and IVV. If ETF1's bid is at least ETF2's ask × κ, buy ETF2 and sell ETF1. Close that position once ETF2's bid is at least ETF1's ask. Do the reverse the same way: if ETF2's bid is at least ETF1's ask × κ, buy ETF1 and sell ETF2, and close once ETF1's bid is at least ETF2's ask. κ is a threshold close to 1, for example 1.002. Execute with fill-or-kill limit orders.
strategies.backtest_note: The backtest needs tick-level synchronized bid/ask quotes and a realistic model of fill-or-kill fills and latency, because these arbitrage opportunities last only a very short time.
data_sources: GAP: synchronized intraday bid/ask quotes for SPY/IVV/VOO
gaps: IBKR historical bid/ask ticks are limited in depth and speed

strategies.name: Index Volatility Targeting with Risk-Free Asset
strategies.name_es: Targeting de volatilidad sobre índice con activo libre de
strategies.rule_summary: Split capital between a stock index and a risk-free asset such as Treasury bills. Put weight w = σ*/σ in the index, where σ* is the target volatility and σ is the index volatility (usually implied, or a volatility forecast), and put 1−w in the risk-free asset. If there is a maximum leverage L, w cannot exceed L. Rebalance on a fixed schedule (weekly, monthly, etc.), or only when the percentage change |Δw|/w since the last rebalance is larger than a threshold κ.
required_data: implied volatility index (e.g. VIX) or volatility forecast
strategies.backtest_note: You have to pick the target σ*, the leverage cap L, the threshold κ and the volatility estimate yourself, because the text gives no values.

strategies.name: VIX Futures Basis Trading
strategies.name_es: Trading de la base de futuros del VIX
strategies.rule_summary: Compute the daily roll D = (UX1 − VIX)/T, where UX1 is the front-month VIX futures price and T is the number of business days to settlement (at least 10). Open a long UX1 position when D < −0.10 (backwardation) and close it when D > −0.05. Open a short UX1 position when D > 0.10 (contango) and close it when D < 0.05. You can hedge volatility spikes with front-month mini-S&P 500 futures, using a hedge ratio from a historical regression of VIX futures price changes on mini-S&P returns.
strategies.backtest_note: The rules are explicit. You need to decide how to roll contracts when fewer than 10 days remain to settlement, and how to estimate the hedge ratio.
data_sources: Cboe CFE VX futures settlement history (public)
gaps: VX trades on CFE, not CME, so roboquant.dev has no data for it

strategies.name: Volatility Carry with Two ETNs
strategies.name_es: Carry de volatilidad con dos ETNs
strategies.rule_summary: Short VXX, which holds short-term VIX futures (months 1-2), and buy VXZ, which holds medium-term VIX futures (months 4-7). This captures the larger roll (contango) loss in VXX. A serial regression of returns sets the hedge ratio between the two ETNs.
required_data: daily close prices of VXX and VXZ
strategies.backtest_note: The text does not specify the regression window or the rebalance frequency, and short-term VXX spikes can cause large drawdowns.
gaps: Original VXX/VXZ ETNs matured in 2019; use relaunched VXX and a mid-term substitute

strategies.name: Hedging Short VXX with VIX Futures
strategies.name_es: Cobertura del VXX con futuros del VIX
strategies.rule_summary: Short VXX and hedge it with a long basket of N mid-maturity VIX futures (for example, 4–7 month maturities, like the VXZ). The basket weights come from a serial regression with intercept of VXX returns on the futures returns, which minimizes tracking error: w_i = σ_X Σ_j C^-1_ij σ_j ρ_j. You can add the constraints w_i ≥ 0 and Σw_i = 1 (dollar-neutral), or minimize total portfolio variance instead. Rebalance monthly or more often.
strategies.backtest_note: The main modelling choices are which futures maturities to use, the estimation window and the weight constraints. Building rolling futures return series also needs care.
gaps: Original VXX/VXZ ETNs matured in 2019; use relaunched VXX and a mid-term substitute

strategies.name: Volatility Risk Premium
strategies.rule_summary: Sell straddles on S&P 500 options to collect the volatility risk premium. As a proxy for the premium, take the VIX at the start of the current month minus the realized volatility (in %) of daily S&P 500 returns since the start of that month. If this spread is positive, sell straddles.
strategies.backtest_note: The text does not give the straddle maturity, strike choice, holding period or how realized vol is measured early in the month, so these must be chosen, and historical SPX option data is needed.
gaps: Needs option quotes

strategies.name: Volatility Risk Premium with Gamma Hedging
strategies.name_es: Prima de riesgo de volatilidad con cobertura de
strategies.rule_summary: Sell ATM straddles (short ATM call and put) on the S&P 500 index to collect the volatility risk premium, as in the base strategy. Keep the position close to Delta-neutral with Gamma hedging: buy the underlying when it moves up and sell it when it moves down. The trade then earns Theta decay on the short options, minus the cost of hedging.
required_data: intraday or daily underlying index prices
strategies.backtest_note: The text gives no maturity, re-hedge frequency or Delta threshold, so the hedging schedule and transaction costs have to be modelled.
gaps: Needs option quotes

strategies.name: Volatility Skew—Long Risk Reversal
strategies.rule_summary: Buy OTM call options and sell OTM put options on the same underlying (a long risk reversal). The trade collects the volatility skew, since OTM puts usually carry higher implied volatility than OTM calls at the same distance from the strike. The position is directional: it loses money if the underlying falls below the put strike minus the net premium received.
strategies.backtest_note: The text gives no strike distance, maturity, holding period or roll rule, so a backtest has to pick these itself and needs historical option data.
gaps: Needs option quotes

strategies.name: Volatility Trading with Variance Swaps
strategies.name_es: Trading de volatilidad con swaps de varianza
strategies.rule_summary: Go long a variance swap when you expect future realized volatility to be higher than current implied volatility. Go short when you expect it to be lower. At maturity T the swap pays N × (v(T) − K), where v(T) is the annualized realized variance from daily log returns (F = 252, mean not subtracted) and K is the preset variance strike. This removes the need to delta-hedge. One example is dispersion: sell a variance swap on an index and buy variance swaps on its constituents.
strategies.backtest_note: Variance swaps trade OTC, so you need historical strike quotes or a model (e.g., to replicate them from option chains). The text gives no explicit signal for when to go long or short.
data_sources: GAP: variance swap quotes (OTC) or option strips for replication
gaps: OTC instrument

strategies.name: Moving Averages with HP Filter
strategies.rule_summary: Apply the Hodrick-Prescott filter to the FX spot rate series (usually monthly data over several years) to remove high-frequency noise and keep the low-frequency trend S*(t). A typical smoothing parameter is λ = 100×n², with n = 12 for monthly data. Compute a short moving average MA(T1) and a long moving average MA(T2), T1 < T2, on S*(t). Buy the currency pair when MA(T1) > MA(T2) and sell when MA(T1) < MA(T2).
strategies.backtest_note: The text does not give T1 or T2. The two-sided HP filter uses future data, so a backtest must re-estimate it at each step using only past data (one-sided) to avoid look-ahead bias.
data_sources: IBKR history (IDEALPRO FX bars or CME FX futures)

strategies.name: Carry Trade
strategies.rule_summary: Sell FX forwards on currencies at a forward premium (forward rate F(t,T) above spot S(t), i.e. low-interest-rate currencies). Buy forwards on currencies at a forward discount (F(t,T) below spot, i.e. high-interest-rate currencies). This is the same as borrowing low-rate currencies and lending high-rate currencies without hedging the FX risk. Positions are held to the forward maturity T and then rolled.
required_data: short-term risk-free interest rates by currency
strategies.backtest_note: The text does not give the forward tenor, how many currencies to trade or how to weight them. Forward prices are OTC, but they can be built from spot rates and interest rates using covered interest parity.
gaps: Nautilus has no FX forward type; model carry as a daily rate-differential accrual or use CME FX futures

strategies.name: High-minus-low Carry
strategies.rule_summary: For each foreign currency, compute the forward discount D = ln(spot) − ln(forward), which is roughly the foreign minus the domestic interest rate. Buy forwards on currencies in the top quantile by forward discount and sell forwards on currencies in the matching bottom quantile, making a zero-cost, dollar-neutral portfolio. The example uses one-month forwards, so the portfolio is rolled and rebalanced monthly.
required_data: short-term interest rates by currency (alternative to forwards)
strategies.backtest_note: FX forwards trade over the counter, so the backtest needs forward quotes or forward rates built from interest-rate differentials, and the quantile cutoff must be chosen.
gaps: Nautilus has no FX forward type; model carry as a daily rate-differential accrual or use CME FX futures

strategies.name: Dollar Carry Trade
strategies.rule_summary: Compute the average forward discount D(t,T) across a basket of N foreign currencies, where each forward discount compares the forward rate with the spot rate. If the average is positive, go long the forwards of all N foreign currencies with equal weights. If it is negative, go short all of them with equal weights. The forward maturity T can be 1, 2, 3, 6 or 12 months, and the position is reset at each maturity.
required_data: FX forward rates by tenor (1-12 months)
strategies.backtest_note: FX forwards trade over the counter, so you need forward quotes or must build them from interest-rate differentials, and you have to pick the currency basket.
gaps: Nautilus has no FX forward type; model carry as a daily rate-differential accrual or use CME FX futures

strategies.name: Momentum and Carry Combo
strategies.rule_summary: Run the FX momentum strategy (Section 8.1) and the FX carry strategy (Section 8.2) together and combine them. One simple way is an equal-weight combo. Another sets the weights w1 and w2 (summing to 1) to minimize the historical variance of the combined return, using sample variances and correlation of the two strategies' returns: w1 = (σ2² − σ1σ2ρ)/(σ1² + σ2² − 2σ1σ2ρ), w2 = (σ1² − σ1σ2ρ)/(σ1² + σ2² − 2σ1σ2ρ).
required_data: FX forward rates or interest rate differentials
historical returns of momentum and carry strategies
strategies.backtest_note: FX forward prices are OTC data, and the user has to choose the estimation window and rebalance schedule for the weights.
gaps: Nautilus has no FX forward type; model carry as a daily rate-differential accrual or use CME FX futures

strategies.name: FX Triangular Arbitrage
strategies.rule_summary: Use three currencies A, B, C and compute the round-trip rate R(A→B→C→A) = Bid(A→B) × Bid(B→C) / Ask(C→A). If R > 1, exchange A for B, B for C, and C back to A to lock in a profit. Check the reverse chain (A→C→B→A) the same way.
required_data: synchronized tick data for three currency pairs
strategies.backtest_note: These opportunities last only moments, so a backtest needs synchronized, executable tick-level bid/ask quotes and a realistic model of latency and fills.
gaps: Profit depends on latency; bar data cannot test it

strategies.name: Roll Yields
strategies.rule_summary: For each commodity, compute phi = P1/P2, where P1 is the front-month futures price and P2 is the second-month futures price. phi > 1 means backwardation and phi < 1 means contango. Build a zero-cost long-short portfolio: go long the futures with higher phi and short the futures with lower phi. Roll the contracts into later maturities as they near expiry.
required_data: daily futures prices for roll returns
strategies.backtest_note: The text does not specify the quantile cutoffs, the weighting, or the rebalance and roll timing, so you have to choose these yourself.
data_sources: IBKR history (expired futures, about 2 years back)
Databento CME (via roboquant.dev or direct; rights decision)
gaps: Long history of individual expiries needs Databento or another CME source

strategies.name: Trading Based on Hedging Pressure
strategies.name_es: Trading basado en la presión de cobertura
strategies.rule_summary: For each commodity, compute hedging pressure (HP) separately for hedgers and speculators from the weekly CFTC COT report: long contracts divided by total long plus short contracts. Split the universe into top and bottom halves by speculators' HP. Buy futures in the top half that are also in the bottom quintile of hedgers' HP, and sell futures in the bottom half that are also in the top quintile of hedgers' HP. The result is a zero-cost portfolio, with formation and holding periods typically 6 months each.
required_data: CFTC COT weekly positions (hedgers/commercial and speculators/non-commercial, long and short)
strategies.backtest_note: COT data is public, but you still have to choose how to average HP over the 6-month formation window, how to roll the futures, and how to deal with a small universe where the double sort leaves few names.
gaps: COT is weekly with a 3-day release lag; use release dates

strategies.name: Portfolio Diversification with Commodities
strategies.rule_summary: Add commodities to a stock portfolio because commodities have low correlation with equities. Passive approach: put a fixed share of capital into commodities, hold, and rebalance back to the target weights on a set schedule (for example, monthly or yearly). Active approach: raise commodity exposure when the Fed discount rate goes up and cut it when the rate goes down, or use some other timing method.
strategies.backtest_note: The text gives no allocation percentages and no exact size of the tilt for the active rule, so these must be picked by the tester.
data_sources: IBKR history (futures or commodity ETF bars)
gaps: Continuous futures need a roll rule

strategies.name: Value
strategies.rule_summary: For each commodity, compute value as v = P5/P0, where P5 is the spot price 5 years ago and P0 is the current spot price. Build a zero-cost portfolio that buys commodities in the top value tercile and sells those in the bottom tercile. Rebalance monthly.
required_data: monthly commodity spot prices (5+ years history)
strategies.backtest_note: Spot prices are often proxied by front-month futures, often averaged around the 5-year-ago date, and positions are taken in futures that must be rolled.
data_sources: IBKR history (futures or commodity ETF bars)
gaps: Continuous futures need a roll rule

strategies.name: Skewness Premium
strategies.rule_summary: For each commodity future, compute the skewness of its historical returns over T observations. Go long the futures in the bottom skewness quintile and short those in the top quintile, which gives a zero-cost portfolio. The section does not give the lookback length or the rebalancing frequency.
strategies.backtest_note: You must choose the skewness lookback window, the rebalance frequency (monthly is assumed here) and the roll method, because the text does not specify them.
data_sources: IBKR history (futures or commodity ETF bars)
gaps: Continuous futures need a roll rule

strategies.name: Trading with Pricing Models
strategies.rule_summary: Model the log spot price of a commodity as a mean-reverting Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. Fit its parameters (mean-reversion speed κ, long-run mean a, volatility σ) to historical futures term-structure data, for example with nonlinear least squares, and compute the model futures price for each maturity. Buy futures whose market price is below the model price (cheap) and sell futures whose market price is above it (rich). Check that the model also predicts well out of sample.
strategies.backtest_note: The text does not specify the calibration window, how big a mispricing must be to trade, position sizing, or how often to rebalance, so these modelling choices must be made by the user.
data_sources: GAP: inventory/storage data for the pricing model
gaps: Pricing-model inputs are not specified

strategies.name: Hedging Risk with Futures
strategies.rule_summary: A trader who expects to buy (sell) a quantity X of a commodity at a future time T buys (sells) at time t a futures contract with delivery date T for that quantity. This locks in the price and hedges the risk of a price rise (fall) between t and T. The position is held until T.
required_data: planned physical purchase/sale quantities and dates
strategies.backtest_note: The hedge depends on an assumed physical exposure (quantity and date), so it can only be tested as hedge effectiveness against that assumed exposure, not as a standalone strategy.
data_sources: IBKR history (futures and the hedged asset)
gaps: This is a hedge overlay; test it as variance reduction, not as a stand-alone return stream

strategies.name: Cross-Hedging
strategies.rule_summary: To hedge an asset that has no futures contract of its own, the trader holds the asset and shorts a futures contract on a different asset with similar characteristics, keeping the position until maturity T. The base case uses a hedge ratio of 1. In practice the optimal hedge ratio is estimated, for example with a time-series regression of spot price changes on futures price changes.
required_data: historical price series for hedge ratio regression
strategies.backtest_note: This is a hedge, not a return-seeking rule: the hedged asset, the proxy future and the hedge-ratio method all have to be chosen by the user.
data_sources: IBKR history (futures and the hedged asset)
gaps: This is a hedge overlay; test it as variance reduction, not as a stand-alone return stream

strategies.name: Interest Rate Risk Hedging
strategies.name_es: Cobertura de riesgo de tasa de interés
strategies.rule_summary: Hedge interest rate risk on a fixed-income position with interest rate futures. Buy futures (long hedge) to protect against falling rates, or sell futures (short hedge) to protect against rising rates. Set the hedge ratio with the conversion factor model (h = C × MB/MF, used for deliverable bonds) or with the modified-duration model (h = β × DB/DF, where DB and DF are dollar durations and β is often 1). The hedge P&L is the change in the futures basis.
strategies.backtest_note: This is a hedging overlay, not a standalone alpha rule, and the text gives no rebalancing schedule or β estimation method.
data_sources: IBKR history (futures and the hedged asset)
gaps: This is a hedge overlay; test it as variance reduction, not as a stand-alone return stream

strategies.name: Calendar Spread
strategies.rule_summary: A bull spread buys the nearby futures contract and sells a deferred-month contract on the same underlying. A bear spread does the reverse. The trader opens a bull spread when they expect low supply and high demand, and a bear spread when they expect high supply and low demand. The idea is that nearby commodity contracts react more strongly than deferred contracts to changes in supply and demand.
strategies.backtest_note: The signal is a discretionary view on supply and demand, so a backtest needs a fundamental forecast model that the text does not specify.
data_sources: IBKR history (expired futures, about 2 years back)
gaps: Individual expiries over long history

strategies.name: Contrarian Trading (Mean-Reversion)
strategies.rule_summary: Compute each future's return over the last week and the equal-weighted market return Rm across N futures. Set weights wi = -γ(Ri - Rm), with γ chosen so the absolute weights sum to 1. This buys the losers and sells the winners relative to the index, and the portfolio is dollar-neutral. Weights may be scaled by 1/σi or 1/σi² (historical volatility) to avoid over-investing in volatile futures. Rebalance weekly.
strategies.backtest_note: You need continuous futures series with rollover rules, and you must choose the futures universe and the volatility lookback window.
gaps: Continuous futures need a roll rule

strategies.name: Contrarian Trading—Market Activity
strategies.rule_summary: Each week, compute the volume factor v = ln(V/V0) for each future, where V is the sum of daily volume over the last week and V0 is the sum over the week before. Compute the open-interest factor u = ln(U/U0) the same way. Keep the futures in the top half by v, then within that set keep the bottom half by u. Apply the basic contrarian rule to this subset: weights equal minus the scaled deviation of each future's last-week return from the cross-sectional mean. This means buying recent losers and shorting recent winners, rebalanced weekly.
strategies.backtest_note: The modeller must choose a contract roll method and how to build continuous volume and open-interest series across contracts.
data_sources: GAP: daily open interest per contract (Databento statistics or exchange data)
gaps: Open interest history

strategies.name: Trend Following (Momentum)
strategies.rule_summary: For each futures contract, compute the cumulative return R_i over a lookback period T (days, weeks or months) and set the signal eta_i = sign(R_i). Set weights w_i = gamma * eta_i / sigma_i, where sigma_i is historical volatility and gamma makes the absolute weights sum to 1. Optional variants: smooth the signal with eta_i = tanh(R_i/kappa); make the book dollar-neutral by demeaning the weights, or by using separate scale factors gamma+ and gamma- for longs and shorts; or use returns net of the market-index return so that winners are bought and losers are sold relative to the index.
strategies.backtest_note: The text leaves the lookback period, rebalance frequency and futures roll method open, so the user has to choose them.
gaps: Continuous futures need a roll rule

strategies.name: Carry, Equity Tranche—Index Hedging
strategies.name_es: Carry, tramo de capital – cobertura con índice
strategies.rule_summary: Buy (sell protection on) the equity tranche, the lowest-quality tranche of a CDO, and delta-hedge it by selling (buying protection on) the underlying CDS index. The hedge ratio is Delta = D / D_ix, the tranche duration divided by the index duration. The strategy earns carry because the equity tranche premiums are larger than the index premiums. The main risk is credit events hitting the equity tranche.
strategies.backtest_note: Needs OTC tranche and index pricing plus a model to compute durations, and the text gives no rebalance rule.
data_sources: GAP: CDX/iTraxx tranche and index quotes, MBS prices
gaps: OTC structured credit; no data source and no instrument type

strategies.name: Carry, Senior/Mezzanine—Index Hedging
strategies.rule_summary: Sell protection on a high-quality CDO tranche (senior or mezzanine). Hedge to Delta-neutrality by buying protection on the underlying CDS index. The hedge ratio is the tranche Delta, i.e. the sensitivity of the tranche value to the index spread.
required_data: default correlation / pricing model inputs for tranche Delta
strategies.backtest_note: You need OTC tranche and index price data plus a pricing model, such as Gaussian copula, to compute the Delta. No rebalance frequency is given; daily is an assumption.
data_sources: GAP: CDX/iTraxx tranche and index quotes, MBS prices
gaps: OTC structured credit; no data source and no instrument type

strategies.name: Carry—Tranche Hedging
strategies.rule_summary: Buy a low-quality (junior) CDO tranche and hedge its delta by selling a high-quality (senior) tranche. The hedge ratio is the risky duration of the low tranche divided by the risky duration of the high tranche (Δ_high = D_low / D_high). The position earns the carry (spread difference) between the two tranches.
strategies.backtest_note: The trade needs OTC tranche prices, and the risky durations have to come from a model; the text gives no rebalancing rule.
data_sources: GAP: CDX/iTraxx tranche and index quotes, MBS prices
gaps: OTC structured credit; no data source and no instrument type

strategies.name: Carry—CDS Hedging
strategies.rule_summary: Buy (sell protection on) a low-quality CDO tranche to collect its high premiums. Hedge the position's delta by buying protection on a single-name CDS whose premiums are lower than the tranche's, rather than hedging with the index or a higher-quality tranche. The hedge ratio is the tranche's risky duration D divided by the CDS risky duration D_CDS (Eq. 489).
required_data: risky durations of tranche and CDS
strategies.backtest_note: You need OTC tranche and CDS prices plus a model for risky durations, and the text gives no rebalancing schedule.
data_sources: GAP: CDX/iTraxx tranche and index quotes, MBS prices
gaps: OTC structured credit; no data source and no instrument type

strategies.name: CDOs—Curve Trades
strategies.rule_summary: To trade a flattener, buy short-maturity protection on a CDO tranche and sell long-maturity protection on the same tranche. This pays off if the spread between long and short maturities narrows. A steepener is the reverse trade. The two legs can be sized to be notional-neutral, risky-duration-neutral or carry-neutral, and P&L is the difference between the mark-to-market values of the long and short legs.
strategies.backtest_note: CDO tranche prices are OTC, so they are hard to get, and the text gives no entry or exit signal. You must choose the timing rule and the neutrality weighting yourself.
data_sources: GAP: CDX/iTraxx tranche and index quotes, MBS prices
gaps: OTC structured credit; no data source and no instrument type

strategies.name: Mortgage-Backed Security (MBS) Trading
strategies.rule_summary: Buy a passthrough MBS and hedge its interest-rate exposure with interest rate swaps. The hedge ratio is the first derivative of the MBS price P with respect to the 5-year swap rate R. You can get it from a prepayment model, or estimate it non-parametrically from historical data with a constrained regression where P is a non-increasing function of R. The text gives no rebalance rule, so you update the hedge as the estimated derivative changes.
strategies.backtest_note: You need OTC MBS and swap prices, and the hedge ratio depends on the choice of prepayment model or regression setup; the text gives no rebalance frequency.
data_sources: GAP: CDX/iTraxx tranche and index quotes, MBS prices
gaps: OTC structured credit; no data source and no instrument type

strategies.name: Convertible Arbitrage
strategies.rule_summary: Buy a newly issued convertible bond, which tends to be underpriced at issuance. At the same time, short h = Δ × C shares of the underlying stock, where C is the conversion ratio and Δ = ∂V/∂S is the model-dependent delta of the conversion option. Rebalance the hedge ratio daily and hold the position for 6 to 12 months from the issue date.
required_data: convertible bond prices and terms (conversion ratio, issue date)
stock volatility and interest rates for a convertible pricing model
strategies.backtest_note: Convertible bond prices trade OTC and are hard to obtain, and the delta depends on which pricing model you choose.
data_sources: GAP: convertible bond prices and terms
gaps: Convertibles are not in our data or Nautilus instrument set

strategies.name: Convertible Option-Adjusted Spread
strategies.name_es: Diferencial ajustado por opciones de convertible
strategies.rule_summary: Take two convertible bonds from the same issuer. Buy the one with the higher option-adjusted spread (OAS) and short the one with the lower OAS, and profit if the two spreads converge. To get the OAS, price the convertible as P_C = P_B + V, where P_B is the straight bond value and V is the call option value. Then shift the Treasury zero-coupon curve in parallel (for example with bisection) until V = P_C(market) − P_B. That parallel shift is the OAS.
required_data: underlying stock prices and volatility for option pricing
strategies.backtest_note: You need OTC convertible bond prices and a model-dependent OAS calculation, and the text gives no rule for when to exit.
data_sources: GAP: convertible bond prices and terms
gaps: Convertibles are not in our data or Nautilus instrument set

strategies.name: Municipal Bond Tax Arbitrage
strategies.rule_summary: Borrow money and buy tax-exempt municipal bonds. The interest expense is deducted from taxable income (tax shield), so the return is R = r_long − r_short(1 − τ), where r_long is the muni bond yield, r_short is the borrowing rate and τ is the corporate tax rate. Hold the position as long as the after-tax carry stays positive.
strategies.backtest_note: The return comes from tax treatment, so a backtest has to assume a tax rate, a financing rate and that interest is deductible, and muni bond prices are OTC and illiquid.
gaps: Profit depends on the tax status of the investor; not a market backtest

strategies.name: Cross-Border Tax Arbitrage
strategies.rule_summary: This applies to stocks in countries with dividend imputation systems, such as Australia, where domestic investors get dividend tax credits but foreign investors do not. The foreign investor sells the stock cum-dividend and buys it back ex-dividend, because the price drop is expected to be larger than the dividend, about D(1+κ) where κ is the tax credit rate. Instead of selling, the investor can lend the stock to a domestic investor cum-dividend and get it back ex-dividend with a pre-agreed share of the tax credit, or use an equivalent swap.
strategies.backtest_note: You can test the sell/buy-back version on ex-dividend price drops, but the lending and swap versions need private deal terms and tax-law details for each jurisdiction.
gaps: Profit depends on the tax status of the investor; not a market backtest

strategies.name: Cross-Border Tax Arbitrage with Options
strategies.rule_summary: A foreign trader who cannot use the dividend tax credit sells the stock cum-dividend at price S0. At the same time the trader sells a deep in-the-money American put, whose price should already include the tax credit: V_put ≈ K − [S0 − D(1+κ)]. A local holder who can use the credit exercises the put ex-dividend at strike K, so the trader buys the shares back at K. The P&L is S0 + V_put − K = D(1+κ).
strategies.backtest_note: A backtest needs option chains around ex-dividend dates, tax credit rates for each country, and a model of when the put holder exercises early. Whether put prices actually include the tax credit is an assumption that must be checked in the data.
gaps: Profit depends on the tax status of the investor; not a market backtest

strategies.name: Inflation Hedging—Inflation Swaps
strategies.name_es: Cobertura contra la inflación – swaps de inflación
strategies.rule_summary: Buy an inflation swap to go long inflation: pay a fixed rate K (the breakeven, usually the Treasury minus TIPS yield spread at the same maturity) and receive a floating rate based on CPI. Sell the swap to take the opposite position. In a zero-coupon swap there is one net payment at maturity T of (I(T)/I(0) − 1) − ((1+K)^T − 1). In a year-on-year swap the parties exchange I(t)/I(t−1) − 1 against K each year.
required_data: Treasury and TIPS yields by maturity
strategies.backtest_note: Inflation swaps trade OTC, so historical swap quotes are hard to get, and the text gives no rule for when to enter or exit; it only describes the hedge structure.
gaps: OTC; TIP versus IEF ETFs is only a rough proxy

strategies.name: TIPS-Treasury Arbitrage
strategies.rule_summary: Short a nominal Treasury bond. Hedge it with a synthetic copy: buy a TIPS with the same maturity, and sell zero-coupon inflation swaps (paying fixed rate K) at each coupon date, with notionals equal to the coupon plus principal at maturity. This turns the CPI-linked payments into fixed ones. Use small long or short STRIPS positions to cover the gap between the Treasury coupons/principal and the synthetic payments. Enter when the net upfront cash flow C(0) = P_Treasury − P_TIPS − sum of STRIPS costs is positive, and hold to maturity, since all later cash flows offset each other.
required_data: zero-coupon inflation swap rates by maturity
strategies.backtest_note: Needs OTC inflation swap quotes and matched TIPS/Treasury/STRIPS prices. Funding and shorting costs also need to be modelled.
data_sources: GAP: TIPS and nominal bond prices, inflation swaps
gaps: Bond-level data

strategies.name: Weather Risk—Demand Hedging
strategies.name_es: Riesgo del clima – cobertura de la demanda
strategies.rule_summary: Build temperature indexes from daily average temperature Ti = (Tmin+Tmax)/2 with Tbase = 65°F: CDD = sum of max(0, Ti − Tbase) and HDD = sum of max(0, Tbase − Ti) over the contract life (week, month or season). Hedge the weather-sensitive part of demand q_w with weather derivatives. For HDD risk, short HDD futures or buy HDD puts. For CDD risk, go long CDD futures or buy CDD calls. Hedge ratios equal Cov(q_w, payoff)/Var(payoff), with the sign as given in the formulas (the put ratio has a minus sign).
strategies.backtest_note: This is a hedge for a company's own demand, not a standalone trading rule. Testing it needs firm-specific demand data and weather-derivative prices, which trade thinly.
gaps: Weather derivatives are illiquid; corporate hedge, not a trading rule

strategies.name: Energy—Spark Spread
strategies.rule_summary: Sell electricity futures and buy natural gas futures to form a spark spread S = PE − H·PF, where H is the plant's heat rate (MMBtu/Mwh). The hedge ratio is h = H·FE/FF, with FE = 736 Mwh and FF = 10,000 MMBtu. Approximate h as a ratio of integers NF/NE with the smallest possible denominator, then buy NF gas contracts for every NE electricity contracts sold. Producers use the position as a hedge, and speculators use it as a bet on a power plant's margin.
strategies.backtest_note: The text gives no entry, exit or timing rules, so the heat rate and holding period must be assumed. Electricity futures data also differ by region.
data_sources: GAP: power and natural gas futures history (CME/ICE)
gaps: Power futures are not in our data

strategies.name: Buying and Holding Distressed Debt
strategies.name_es: Inversión pasiva en deuda en distress
strategies.rule_summary: Buy the debt of distressed companies at a deep discount and hold it, expecting the company to repay or reorganize successfully. A bond counts as distressed when its yield spread over Treasuries is above a set threshold, for example 1,000 bps. Spread the portfolio across industries, issuers, and debt seniority and quality. Positions are often opened on key dates, such as the end of the month of a default or bankruptcy filing, to profit from market overreaction.
strategies.backtest_note: Distressed bonds trade over the counter, so prices are thin and hard to get, and recovery and exit choices need modelling assumptions.
gaps: Bond-level data

strategies.name: Active Distressed Investing
strategies.name_es: Inversión activa en activos en distress
strategies.rule_summary: Buy the debt or other securities of a distressed company to gain some control over how it is managed and reorganized. This differs from the passive approach. The company may reorganize under Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection or work directly with its creditors out of court. The investor uses its stake to influence the reorganization outcome.
strategies.backtest_note: Returns depend on gaining control and on negotiated reorganization outcomes, not on a systematic rule, so a backtest is not possible.
gaps: Active control of a bankrupt company; not a market rule

strategies.name: Planning a Reorganization
strategies.rule_summary: The investor buys a substantial stake in a bankrupt company's debt and files a reorganization plan with the bankruptcy court. The aim is to gain some role in running the company, raise its value, and profit. Plans filed by large debt holders tend to be more competitive.
strategies.backtest_note: The strategy depends on active legal involvement and court outcomes, not on a mechanical trading rule.
gaps: Active control of a bankrupt company; not a market rule

strategies.name: Buying Outstanding Debt
strategies.rule_summary: Buy the outstanding debt of a distressed company at a large discount. The bet is that after the reorganization, part of this debt turns into equity, which gives the investor some control over the company.
strategies.backtest_note: This is a discretionary, case-by-case control play built on illiquid OTC debt and negotiated restructuring outcomes, with no explicit systematic rule.
gaps: Active control of a bankrupt company; not a market rule

strategies.name: Loan-to-own
strategies.rule_summary: Lend money through secured loans to a distressed company that is not yet bankrupt. The investor profits if the company recovers, avoids bankruptcy and its equity value rises. If the company files for Chapter 11 instead, the secured loan is converted into equity with control rights during the reorganization.
required_data: company financial condition and credit data
strategies.backtest_note: The strategy depends on privately negotiated secured loans and taking control in a restructuring, so it has no mechanical rule or public price series to test.
gaps: Active control of a bankrupt company; not a market rule

strategies.name: Distress Risk Puzzle
strategies.rule_summary: For each stock, estimate the probability of bankruptcy P_i, for example with a logistic regression. Short the stocks in the top decile of P_i (the riskiest) and buy the stocks in the bottom decile (the safest), which gives a zero-cost portfolio. Rebalance monthly; annual rebalancing is also possible and gives similar returns.
strategies.backtest_note: You must choose and estimate the bankruptcy-probability model (logistic regression), and that requires historical bankruptcy data and fundamentals.
gaps: Failure-probability model inputs must be point-in-time

strategies.name: Distress Risk Puzzle—Risk Management
strategies.name_es: Rompecabezas de riesgo de dificultades – gestión
strategies.rule_summary: Build the standard healthy-minus-distressed (HMD) zero-cost portfolio: go long financially healthy stocks and short distressed stocks, ranked by estimated bankruptcy/distress probability. Scale the position by sigma_target / sigma_hat. sigma_target is the target volatility, usually 10%-15%. sigma_hat is the strategy's realized volatility, estimated from daily returns over the past year. If you do not want leverage, cap the scale factor at min(sigma_target/sigma_hat, 1).
required_data: accounting data for distress/bankruptcy probability estimation
strategies.backtest_note: You must choose a distress-probability model (e.g. failure probability or O-score), and this section does not give the rebalance frequency.
gaps: Failure-probability model inputs must be point-in-time

strategies.name: Mixed-Asset Diversification with Real Estate
strategies.name_es: Diversificación de activos mixtos con bienes raíces
strategies.rule_summary: Buy and hold real estate assets as part of a traditional portfolio of stocks and bonds to get diversification, because real estate has low correlation with other assets. Set the weights with mean-variance optimization or a vector autoregressive (VAR) model, based on the investor's risk/return preferences and time horizon.
required_data: real estate return series (REIT or property index)
strategies.backtest_note: You can backtest this with REIT indexes, but you must choose the weights yourself (the optimizer, the horizon, and the investor's preferences), and direct property returns are appraisal-based.
data_sources: IBKR history (REIT ETF proxies, e.g. VNQ)
gaps: REIT ETFs are a proxy for direct real estate

strategies.name: Intra-asset Diversification Within Real Estate
strategies.rule_summary: Spread real estate holdings across several properties that differ by geographic area, property type, size, distance to a metropolitan area, and economic region. Allocation weights come from standard portfolio construction methods such as mean-variance optimization, as in Section 16.2.
required_data: property-level or regional real estate return indices
strategies.backtest_note: Physical properties are illiquid and have appraisal-based returns, so a backtest needs REIT or regional index proxies and a chosen allocation method.
data_sources: GAP: property-type and regional real-estate return indexes (e.g. NCREIF)
gaps: Index returns are appraisal-based and not tradable

strategies.name: Property Type Diversification
strategies.name_es: Diversificación por el tipo de propiedad
strategies.rule_summary: Hold a real estate portfolio spread across property types such as apartments, offices, industrial properties (including manufacturing buildings), and retail shopping centers. The aim is to lower non-systematic risk. The text gives no weighting or rebalancing rules.
required_data: property returns by property type (e.g., appraisal-based indices or sector REIT returns)
strategies.backtest_note: Physical property is illiquid and the rule gives no weights, so a backtest needs proxies such as sector REITs or property-type indices plus an assumed allocation scheme.
data_sources: GAP: property-type and regional real-estate return indexes (e.g. NCREIF)
gaps: Index returns are appraisal-based and not tradable

strategies.name: Economic Diversification
strategies.rule_summary: Spread real estate investments across regions that are grouped by economic traits, such as main economic activity, employment statistics and average income. The goal is to cut non-systematic risk and transaction costs. The text gives no weighting or rebalancing rule.
required_data: regional economic indicators (employment, income, industry mix)
strategies.backtest_note: Direct property data is illiquid and appraisal-based, and the text gives no rule for defining regions or setting weights, so a test has to rely on proxies such as regional REIT indices.
data_sources: GAP: property-type and regional real-estate return indexes (e.g. NCREIF)
gaps: Index returns are appraisal-based and not tradable

strategies.name: Property Type and Geographic Diversification
strategies.name_es: Diversificación por el tipo de propiedad y la región
strategies.rule_summary: Build a real estate portfolio diversified across two attributes at once, property type and geographic region. For example, with four property types (office, retail, industrial, residential) and four US regions (East, Midwest, South, West), spread holdings across the 16 resulting groups.
required_data: property-level returns or values by type and region
strategies.backtest_note: This applies to physical property portfolios and gives no weighting rule, so a backtest would need appraisal-based indices or REITs as proxies plus a chosen weighting scheme (e.g. equal weight).
data_sources: GAP: property-type and regional real-estate return indexes (e.g. NCREIF)
gaps: Index returns are appraisal-based and not tradable

strategies.name: Real Estate Momentum—Regional Approach
strategies.rule_summary: Buy real estate in the US metropolitan statistical areas (MSAs) with the highest past returns, because past winners tend to keep outperforming and past losers tend to keep underperforming. You can build a zero-cost version by going long high-momentum regions and short low-momentum regions through REITs, or through futures and options on regional US house price indexes. The text gives no lookback period and no rebalance schedule.
strategies.backtest_note: You cannot trade physical property directly, so you must use regional REITs or thinly traded house price index derivatives as proxies, and you have to choose the lookback and rebalance periods yourself.
data_sources: GAP: property-type and regional real-estate return indexes (e.g. NCREIF)
gaps: Index returns are appraisal-based and not tradable

strategies.name: Inflation Hedging with Real Estate
strategies.name_es: Cobertura contra la inflación con bienes raíces
strategies.rule_summary: Hold real estate as a hedge against inflation, because studies find real estate returns track the inflation rate. Commercial real estate may hedge better than other property types, since its prices adjust faster to inflation. The text gives no explicit entry, exit or rebalance rules.
required_data: real estate returns by property type
strategies.backtest_note: The section only says real estate tends to rise with inflation and gives no trading rule, so testing it means using REITs or appraisal-based indices in place of physical property.
data_sources: GAP: property-type and regional real-estate return indexes (e.g. NCREIF)
gaps: Index returns are appraisal-based and not tradable

strategies.name: Fix-and-flip
strategies.rule_summary: Buy a run-down property that needs renovation at a substantial discount to market price. Renovate it, then resell it at a price high enough to cover the renovation costs and leave a profit.
strategies.backtest_note: The strategy trades individual physical properties and depends on deal-specific renovation work, so it cannot be backtested systematically.
gaps: Not a tradable market strategy

strategies.name: Money Laundering—The Dark Side of Cash
strategies.name_es: Lavado de dinero – el lado oscuro del efectivo
strategies.rule_summary: This is not a trading rule. The section describes money laundering in three steps: placement (illegal cash is split into small deposits across many bank accounts), layering (the money is moved between accounts and countries to hide where it came from), and integration (the money comes back through cash-heavy businesses such as bars, restaurants, car washes and casinos). There are no positions, signals or exit rules.
strategies.backtest_note: This is an illegal activity, only described, with no market rule to test.
gaps: Describes money laundering, which is illegal. Excluded.

strategies.name: Liquidity Management
strategies.rule_summary: Keep the best amount of cash in the portfolio to cover liquidity needs from unexpected events, so other assets do not have to be sold at high transaction cost. Companies can also hold cash as a precaution against cash-flow shortfalls. The text gives no explicit rule for choosing the cash level.
strategies.backtest_note: This is a general idea about how much cash to hold, with no explicit trading rule or parameters to test.
gaps: Not a tradable market strategy

strategies.name: Repurchase Agreement (REPO)
strategies.rule_summary: Borrow cash at a fixed interest rate for a set term (repo) by posting assets as collateral and agreeing to buy them back from the counterparty, or lend cash against collateral and agree to sell it back (reverse repo). Terms usually run from 1 day to 6 months.
strategies.backtest_note: The text only describes a cash-equivalent funding transaction and gives no selection or timing rule to test.
gaps: Not a tradable market strategy

strategies.name: Pawnbroking
strategies.rule_summary: The lender gives a cash loan that carries interest and has a pre-agreed term, which can sometimes be extended. The loan is secured by valuable items such as jewelry, electronics, vehicles, rare books or musical instruments. The loan amount is usually well below the appraised value of the collateral. If the borrower does not repay on the agreed terms, the lender keeps or sells the collateral.
strategies.backtest_note: This is private secured lending against physical goods, so there is no market price data for a backtest.
gaps: Not a tradable market strategy

strategies.name: Loan Sharking
strategies.rule_summary: The lender makes loans at very high interest rates, often with no collateral, and sometimes uses blackmail or violence to make borrowers repay. There is no trading rule for selecting securities, entering, or exiting.
strategies.backtest_note: This is an illegal private lending activity, not a market trading rule, so there is no price data to backtest.
gaps: Loan sharking is illegal in many places. Excluded.

strategies.name: Artificial Neural Network (ANN)
strategies.rule_summary: Train an artificial neural network to forecast short-term Bitcoin moves, e.g. on 15-minute bars. Inputs are technical indicators built from mean-adjusted, volatility-normalized returns: the normalized return itself, EMAs and EMSDs with lengths of 30 min, 1 h, 3 h and 6 h, and RSIs with lengths of 3 h, 6 h and 12 h. The output layer predicts which of K quantiles the next normalized return will fall into, and you trade BTC long or short in the direction of the predicted quantile.
strategies.backtest_note: You must choose the network design, the training window, the number of quantiles and the signal-to-trade mapping yourself, and the many free parameters make overfitting likely.
data_sources: Crypto exchange public OHLCV (Nautilus has exchange adapters)
gaps: Model training needs a walk-forward split to avoid look-ahead

strategies.name: Sentiment Analysis—Naïve Bayes Bernoulli
strategies.name_es: Análisis de sentimiento – naïve Bayes Bernoulli
strategies.rule_summary: Collect tweets that contain keywords from a BTC-related vocabulary over a time period, clean them (remove duplicates and stop words, apply stemming), and encode each tweet as a binary (Bernoulli) feature vector showing which vocabulary words appear in it. A naïve Bayes classifier trained on past data estimates the conditional probability of each class, for example BTC going up or down, or quantiles of normalized returns. The trade goes in the direction of the most likely class: buy when up is predicted and sell when down is predicted.
strategies.backtest_note: A backtest needs historical Twitter data plus your own choices for the vocabulary, the text cleaning, the prediction horizon and the class definitions, and the text does not specify any of these.
data_sources: GAP: historical tweet text for BTC keywords
gaps: No tweet archive

strategies.name: Fundamental Macro Momentum
strategies.rule_summary: For each country, compute 1-year trends in four macro state variables: business cycle (1-year change in real GDP growth and expected CPI, 50% weight each), international trade (1-year change in FX spot vs an export-weighted basket), monetary policy (1-year change in short-term rates), and risk sentiment (1-year equity market excess return). Rank assets within each class (e.g., country equity indexes, currencies, government bonds) by these scores, using the sign that matches how each trend affects that asset class. Go long the top decile and short the bottom decile. Combine the asset-class portfolios with equal weights and hold each position for 3 to 6 months.
required_data: FX spot rates and export weights
equity index returns and risk-free rates
strategies.backtest_note: The text does not say how to combine the four variables or set the sign for each asset class, and the expected-CPI and macro data must be point-in-time.
data_sources: FRED / OECD macro series (with release dates)
IBKR history (country index, bond and FX futures/ETFs)
gaps: Macro data must be vintage (as first released)

strategies.name: Global Macro Inflation Hedge
strategies.name_es: Cobertura macro global contra la inflación
strategies.rule_summary: Set the commodity share of the portfolio to CA = max(0, min((HI_YoY − CI_YoY)/HI_YoY, 1)), where HI is year-over-year headline inflation and CI is year-over-year core inflation. Take the commodity exposure by buying a basket of commodities through ETFs or futures. Recompute the share whenever new inflation data is released.
strategies.backtest_note: The text does not specify the commodity basket, what the rest of the portfolio holds, or how to handle inflation data release lags.
data_sources: FRED / OECD macro series (with release dates)
IBKR history (country index, bond and FX futures/ETFs)
gaps: Macro data must be vintage (as first released)

strategies.name: Global Fixed-Income Strategy
strategies.rule_summary: Rank government bonds (usually country bond ETFs) of different countries cross-sectionally on macro and market factors: GDP, inflation, sovereign risk, real interest rates, output gap, value, momentum, yield-curve term spread, and the Cochrane-Piazzesi predictor. Buy the bonds in the top quantile and sell those in the bottom quantile to form a zero-cost portfolio. You can also combine several factors into a multifactor ranking.
required_data: sovereign risk measures (e.g. CDS spreads or ratings)
strategies.backtest_note: The text does not specify how to define the factors, how to combine them, the quantile cutoffs, or the rebalance frequency, so the monthly frequency is an assumption; cross-country macro data must also be aligned with release dates.
data_sources: FRED / OECD macro series (with release dates)
IBKR history (country index, bond and FX futures/ETFs)
gaps: Macro data must be vintage (as first released)

strategies.name: Trading on Economic Announcements
strategies.rule_summary: Hold 100% in equities (through an index ETF or equity index futures) on days with major economic announcements, such as FOMC announcements. On all other days, hold 100% in risk-free assets (Treasury bills or bonds). You can add filters, for example technical filters.
required_data: FOMC and other macro announcement calendar
strategies.backtest_note: The text does not define which announcements count as major, and it does not say exactly when to enter and exit around each announcement day.
